title: The Corporate Fraud
description: £2.5M was siphoned through ghost invoices to a Cayman offshore account.
solution_summary: CFO Richard Sterling signed off fake transfers and routed funds to his Cayman shell company.

suspects.name: Richard Sterling
suspects.motive: Heavy debts and luxury yacht expenses.
suspects.alibi: Claims an external hacker spoofed his credentials.
suspects.statement: Our network was breached! A hacker spoofed my login!
contradictions: Hardware 2FA token used for authorization was in Richard's physical pocket.

suspects.name: Elena Rostova
suspects.alibi: On verified maternity leave.
suspects.statement: I reported the invoice anomalies as soon as I returned.

suspects.name: Thomas Vance
suspects.alibi: In server room with logged CCTV.
suspects.statement: I flagged the abnormal wire within minutes of execution.

evidence.name: Offshore Wire Ledger
evidence.description: Wire records routing £2.5M to Apex Horizons Ltd, owned by Richard Sterling.
evidence.details: Apex Horizons registration directly lists Richard Sterling as owner.

evidence.name: Hardware 2FA Security Token
evidence.description: Physical RSA token in Richard office used to authorize the transfer.
evidence.details: Token was active in Richard office at transfer time.

evidence.name: Deleted Email Archive
evidence.description: Recovered emails instructing offshore agents to liquidate funds.
evidence.details: Emails sent from Richard private workstation.

evidence.name: Forged Vendor Invoice
evidence.description: Fake software invoice stamped with CFO approval.
evidence.details: Signature matches CFO approval stamps.

evidence.name: Encrypted USB Drive
evidence.description: USB found in executive desk containing offshore bank keys.
evidence.details: Contains private keys for Cayman bank account.

rules.name: Unauthorized Fund Transfer
rules.description: Digital credentials matching suspect used for fraudulent transaction.

rules.name: Corporate Embezzlement Conviction
rules.description: Fraudulent transfer directly linked to suspect's offshore account confirms embezzlement.

title: The Missing Necklace
description: Lady Kensington diamond necklace vanished from her private safe during a charity ball.
solution_summary: Marcus Sterling used a duplicate key to steal the necklace and hide it in his appraisal case.

suspects.name: Marcus Sterling
suspects.alibi: Appraising silverware in the conservatory.
suspects.statement: I was admiring silverware all night. I never went near the safe!
contradictions: Necklace appraisal velvet cloth found in Marcus's valise.

suspects.name: Duchess Vivienne
suspects.motive: Coveted the necklace for her collection.
suspects.alibi: Singing near the ballroom orchestra.
suspects.statement: I was dancing in the ballroom all evening with the guests.

suspects.name: Higgins
suspects.alibi: Serving wine in the dining hall.
suspects.statement: I served champagne until midnight, witnessed by many.

evidence.name: Opened Wall Safe
evidence.description: Safe opened without damage using a precision duplicate key.
evidence.details: Lock shows zero signs of forced tool entry.

evidence.name: Duplicate Brass Safe Key
evidence.description: Found in Marcus velvet case, matching the Kensington safe.
evidence.details: Cut matches the Kensington wall safe lock cylinder.

evidence.name: Velvet Jewelry Box in Marcus's Bag
evidence.description: Stolen diamond necklace hidden inside Marcus case.
evidence.details: Contains the genuine stolen Kensington diamond necklace.

evidence.name: Guest Registry Log
evidence.description: Log showing Marcus entered private wing at 11:20 PM.
evidence.details: Shows Marcus entered the private quarters during the ball.

evidence.name: Silk Glove Fragment
evidence.description: White thread on vault dial matching Marcus appraisal gloves.
evidence.details: Thread matches white appraisal gloves worn by Marcus.

evidence.name: Ballroom Orchestra Recording
evidence.description: Audio verifying Duchess Vivienne was singing near the band.
evidence.details: Confirms Duchess was in the ballroom continuously.

rules.name: Safe Unauthorized Access
rules.description: Possession of safe key and unforced entry indicates insider access.

rules.name: Possession of Stolen Property
rules.description: Possession of stolen necklace with vault access confirms grand larceny.

title: The Clocktower Sabotage
description: The Westminster Clock was sabotaged and its platinum gear stolen at midnight.
solution_summary: Tobias Vance used his master key to steal the platinum gear to pay debts, leaving filings on his apron.

suspects.name: Tobias Vance
suspects.alibi: Claims he was asleep in the ground floor lodge.
suspects.statement: I was sound asleep in the porter lodge all night.
contradictions: CCTV captures Tobias climbing the tower stairs at 11:55 PM, directly debunking his lodge alibi.
Platinum metal shavings matching the stolen gear were found embedded in Tobias's work apron.

suspects.name: Lady Genevieve
suspects.motive: Wanted the mechanism for her private museum.
suspects.alibi: Attending a charity ball at the Savoy Hotel.
suspects.statement: I was at the Savoy gala all evening. The guest list confirms it.

suspects.name: Alistair Finch
suspects.alibi: Securing the lower bell belfry.
suspects.statement: I made rounds on the belfry level all evening.

suspects.name: Dr. Sterling
suspects.alibi: Reviewing blueprints at the City Council archives.
suspects.statement: I finished my survey at noon and had no business at midnight.

evidence.name: Damaged Gear Mechanism
evidence.description: Drive housing torn open with specialized horology tools.
evidence.details: Removal required professional horological tools.

evidence.name: Master Gear Key
evidence.description: Brass key with initials T.V. found on the gear platform.
evidence.details: Fingerprints on the key match Tobias Vance.

evidence.name: Tower Security Camera Log
evidence.description: CCTV recorded at the internal spiral staircase.
evidence.details: 11:55 PM: Man wearing horologist apron enters gear chamber.

evidence.name: Platinum Metal Filings
evidence.description: Microscopic platinum shavings inside Tobias apron pocket.
evidence.details: Spectrometry confirms shavings match the 950-platinum clock gear.

evidence.name: Blackmail Telegram
evidence.description: Debt collection notice demanding £50,000 within 24 hours.
evidence.details: Sent to Tobias Vance from loan sharks.

rules.name: Tower Access & Opportunity
rules.description: Presence at the clock tower during the sabotage window proves physical opportunity.

rules.name: Physical Theft Entailment
rules.description: Presence combined with physical possession of shavings and fingerprints proves guilt beyond reasonable doubt.

title: The Midnight Murder
description: Arthur Vance was fatally stabbed in his locked study at midnight. Four suspects were present.
solution_summary: Victor Vance entered at 11:50 PM, handled the knife leaving fingerprints, and falsified his cinema alibi.

suspects.name: Victor Vance
suspects.alibi: Claims he attended a late-night cinema screening until 1 AM.
suspects.statement: I was at the cinema downtown all evening! I never touched any knives.
contradictions: CCTV captures Victor entering the mansion at 11:50 PM, directly debunking his cinema alibi.
Victor's fingerprints were identified on the handle of the bloody murder knife.

suspects.name: Clara Sterling
suspects.motive: Threatened with an audit over joint business funds.
suspects.alibi: Working in the library until 11:15 PM, then retired to guest room.
suspects.statement: We argued earlier, but I left Arthur alive in his study.

suspects.name: Arthur Finch
suspects.motive: Given termination notice earlier that morning.
suspects.alibi: Polishing silverware in the basement pantry.
suspects.statement: I served Master Arthur tea at 10:30 PM, then went straight to the pantry.

suspects.name: Dr. Julian Hayes
suspects.motive: Dispute over Arthur medical trust donation.
suspects.alibi: Performing emergency surgery at St. Jude Hospital.
suspects.statement: I was at the hospital in surgery until 2:30 AM. Hospital logs confirm it.

evidence.name: Coroner's Autopsy Report
evidence.description: Victim died from a single stab wound between 11:45 PM and 12:15 AM.
evidence.details: Cause of death: acute blood loss from a 6-inch blade puncture.

evidence.name: Bloody Chef Knife
evidence.description: 6-inch Japanese steel kitchen knife stained with victim blood.
evidence.details: Fingerprints on handle match Victor Vance with 99.8% certainty.

evidence.name: Fingerprints on Brandy Goblet
evidence.description: Half-empty crystal goblet resting on the study side table.
evidence.details: Arthur Vance and Butler Finch fingerprints detected on rim.

evidence.name: Broken Balcony Glass
evidence.description: French balcony doors shattered outward; latch opened from inside.
evidence.details: Fracture analysis confirms latch was opened from inside.

evidence.name: Encrypted Smartphone
evidence.description: Smartphone with urgent SMS communications found in desk drawer.
evidence.details: Message from Victor: If you refuse the estate advance, you will regret it.

evidence.name: CCTV Security Hard Drive
evidence.description: Gate security footage salvaged from estate gatehouse.
evidence.details: Camera 03 captures Victor Vance entering through side gate at 11:50 PM.

evidence.name: Bloodstained Persian Rug
evidence.description: Heavy wool rug beneath desk with distinctive blood splatter.
evidence.details: Blood pattern matches sudden attack while seated behind desk.

evidence.name: Muddy Bootprints
evidence.description: Tread marks near french doors leading from wet garden.
evidence.details: Size 10 leather soles matching shoes found in Victor wardrobe.

rules.name: Physical Contact with Weapon
rules.description: Fingerprints on the knife establish physical contact.

rules.name: Lethal Weapon Identification
rules.description: Stab wound cause of death combined with victim's blood on knife establishes it as the murder weapon.

rules.name: Opportunity and Scene Presence
rules.description: Presence at the scene during time of death establishes opportunity.

rules.name: Alibi Falsification
rules.description: Direct CCTV footage of suspect at the crime scene directly refutes an external alibi.

rules.name: Motive and Intent
rules.description: Threatening messages combined with financial inheritance/debt establish strong motive.

rules.name: Proof of Guilt Beyond Reasonable Doubt
rules.description: All legal requirements satisfied for murder conviction.

title: The Poisoner of St. Jude's
description: Dr. Ward was lethally poisoned with digitalis in his tea in the surgical archives.
solution_summary: Dr. Thaddeus Hayes poisoned Dr. Ward to prevent exposure of research plagiarism.

suspects.name: Dr. Thaddeus Hayes
suspects.motive: Ward discovered Hayes plagiarized his landmark cardiac study.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was in the downstairs cafeteria having tea.
suspects.statement: Archibald was a valued colleague! I was in the cafeteria all evening.
contradictions: Pharmacy biometric log records Thaddeus dispensing pure digitalis extract at 11:32 PM.
Digitalis toxin residue was detected on Thaddeus's latex surgical gloves found in the archive bin.

suspects.name: Nurse Beatrice Vance
suspects.alibi: Dispensing routine medications in Ward 4.
suspects.statement: I was with patients on Ward 4 all night. Every dose is logged.

suspects.name: Leonard Cross
suspects.alibi: Checked out of hospital at 8 PM and stayed at hotel.
suspects.statement: I was furious about the contract, but I left hours before the incident.

suspects.name: Clara Finch
suspects.alibi: Filing records in basement storage.
suspects.statement: I brought Dr. Ward his tea tray at 10:30 PM. He was alive and reading.

evidence.name: Poisoned Silver Teapot
evidence.description: Silver teapot infused with lethal digitalis glycoside.
evidence.details: Dosage was 50x lethal threshold; rapid cardiac arrest within 10 minutes.

evidence.name: Pharmacy Dispenser Biometric Log
evidence.description: Digital access log of restricted poisons cabinet.
evidence.details: Card #409 (Dr. T. Hayes) unlocked digitalis vault at 11:32 PM.

evidence.name: Discarded Surgical Gloves
evidence.description: Latex gloves in archive waste bin with chemical stains.
evidence.details: Digitalis powder and DNA matching Thaddeus Hayes found on lining.

evidence.name: Plagiarism Accusation Letter
evidence.description: Draft letter from Dr. Ward demanding Hayes immediate resignation.
evidence.details: Demands Hayes resign or face criminal fraud charges.

evidence.name: Hospital Corridor Security Pass
evidence.description: Card reader log at archive corridor door 3B.
evidence.details: Records Thaddeus Hayes scanning into archive corridor at 11:40 PM.

rules.name: Poison Procurement & Opportunity
rules.description: Procuring the poison and entering the crime scene during the poisoning window establishes administration.

rules.name: Homicide Conviction
rules.description: Physical chemical proof combined with established motive and administration confirms murder beyond reasonable doubt.

title: The Royal Sovereign Diamond
description: The 200-carat Sovereign Diamond was swapped with a glass fake in the Royal Vault.
solution_summary: Director Raymond Sterling stole the diamond to sell to smugglers, bypassing lasers with his credentials.

suspects.name: Lord Raymond Sterling
suspects.motive: Gaming debts; arranged offshore sale to an illegal antiquities cartel.
suspects.alibi: Claims he attended a diplomatic dinner at the French Embassy.
suspects.statement: I have dedicated my life to the Gallery! I was dining at the Embassy.
contradictions: Biometric vault console shows Raymond's thumbprint override at 11:42 PM.
Diamond dust residue matching the Sovereign Diamond was identified inside Raymond's leather briefcase.

suspects.name: Evelyn Vance
suspects.alibi: Working in university lab under supervision.
suspects.statement: I authenticated the stone at 5 PM, then went straight to my lab.

suspects.name: Marcus Blackwood
suspects.alibi: Stationed at the main gallery security desk.
suspects.statement: I was at the security desk. Lasers were disarmed from director panel.

suspects.name: Baroness von Hayes
suspects.alibi: Attending embassy reception with full diplomatic staff.
suspects.statement: I was surrounded by foreign dignitaries all evening.

evidence.name: Glass Replica Diamond
evidence.description: High-index cubic zirconia crystal left in place of genuine diamond.
evidence.details: Hardness rating 8.0, confirming it is an artificial substitute.

evidence.name: Biometric Vault Override Console
evidence.description: Vault door security panel showing access authentication logs.
evidence.details: Thumbprint #01 (Director Raymond Sterling) logged at 11:42 PM.

evidence.name: Diamond Dust in Leather Briefcase
evidence.description: Diamond facet dust found inside Raymond leather briefcase.
evidence.details: Refraction index matches Sovereign Diamond with zero doubt.

evidence.name: Smuggling Bill of Lading
evidence.description: Cargo manifest for steam cutter departing for Tangier at 2 AM.
evidence.details: Chartered in the name of Raymond Sterling.

evidence.name: Laser Grid Override Tool
evidence.description: Bypass keycard and device found in director office safe.
evidence.details: Configured specifically to bypass vault pressure sensors.

rules.name: Vault Infiltration & Theft
rules.description: Disabling the vault with biometric credentials and swapping the gem proves theft.

rules.name: Grand Larceny Entailment
rules.description: Theft established alongside physical diamond dust and smuggling arrangements confirms guilt beyond reasonable doubt.
